channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Photon-driven magnetization switching in Fe3GeTe2 enables programmable, multilevel magnetic memory
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Horng-Tay Jeng, Chang-Hua Liu

Authors: Wei-Qing Li, Sheng-Hsiung Hung, Jia-Xin Li, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experiments on magnetic van der Waals materials are highly relevant to quantum materials research.

Tags: #magnetism #van-der-waals #photonics

Abstract: This work demonstrates that pulsed optical excitation enables reversible all-optical switching of the magnetic state in Fe₃GeTe₂ and reveals the roles of photon energy, fluence, and polarization in governing the switching behavior

item.title: [9] Observation of a spin-textured nematic Kondo lattice
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Rafael M. Fernandes, M. Zahid Hasan

Authors: Yu-Xiao Jiang, Zi-Jia Cheng, Qiaozhi Xu, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: M. Zahid Hasan

Tags: #scanningtunneling #nematic #Kondo

Abstract: The authors study the layered Kondo magnet USbTe by spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy. They discover a spin-polarized nematic state below 15 K, coinciding with the formation of heavy quasi-particles driven by band hybridization.
